lines.note: Romuru completes hiromuru from f197; the same fragment there is a catchword. The example means propagating God's law, not a separate verb tomuru.
Deos completes lei de Deos, the Christian law or teaching being spread. It is Portuguese rather than a Japanese proper name.
Hiromi is a broad place, paraphrased hiroi tokoro. The paraphrase and scan restore the damaged r in Firomi.
Eſpaçoſo completes the spacious-place definition. No additional Japanese sense starts on this line.
Hiroi niwa is a broad courtyard. Preserve the printed adjective phrase even though the alphabetical position might suggest hironiwa; NINJAL also records the longer form.

runs.text: Aço da Catana que vai con

lines.note: Hirosugu-yakiba describes the broad straight tempered edge of a sword. Catana sits within Portuguese syntax, and con begins continuando below.
The steel or hardened edge continues like a broad long vein. This describes its form rather than a separate sword component to add editorially.
Hiroen is a broad veranda. The short gloss directly confirms the architectural meaning.
Hiru is daytime or midday. Yoru, hiru gives night and day; the draft's extra v before Yoru was not a Japanese syllable.
Dia and noite translate the pair in reversed order. Preserve the dictionary's ordering rather than align it artificially word by word.
The homonym hiru means garlic, equated with ninniku. X limits the recorded usage regionally; it is not part of the Japanese name.
Another hiru denotes a leech. Sambixuga is the printed Portuguese term and is not modernized to sanguessuga.
Hirugaeru means turning or folding back. The following flags-in-wind example establishes the physical sense.

runs.text: as bandeiras, &c. com o vento. ¶ Item,

lines.note: Flags turn in the wind; bandeiras restores the omitted r. Item signals an additional, figurative reversal.

runs.text: Retroceder, ou tornar atras do começado.

lines.note: The figurative meaning is going back from something begun. This is a reversal of course rather than a new motion verb.
Hirugaesu is the transitive counterpart: wind turns flags or sleeves. Eita and vento repair OCR errors in the inflection and Portuguese subject.

runs.text: deiras, mãgas do veſtido, &c. ¶ Item, Perm.

lines.note: Flags and clothing sleeves complete the objects. The editorial Perm. introduces a metaphorical application.
Yakusoku wo hirugaesu is undoing an agreement. Cõcerto, not cõterto, names that agreement in the Portuguese gloss.
Zonbun wo hirugaesu is changing one's opinion. Zombũ preserves the abbreviated nasal spelling while the spurious split before ſu is removed.

runs.text: Comparação: não ſe vſa por ſi, ſe não cõ-

lines.note: Hirui means comparison or a comparable counterpart, and is said not to stand alone. The next example supplies the compound construction.
Hirui nai tegara ja is an unequalled feat. Nai, not naa, is the negation supported by the Japanese and the scan.
The feat has no equal, completing façanha. This confirms the comparative meaning of hirui above.
The homonymous hirui means sorrowful tears, explained by kanashimu namida. It is not the comparison noun from the preceding entry.
Hirui ni shizumu means sinking in tears of sorrow. The Portuguese bathing-in-tears metaphor translates that image.
Em lagrimas de tristeza completes the tearful state. OCR's initial d in dagrimas was a misread l.
Hiru-ii, written Firuiy, is the midday rice meal, equated with hirumeshi. The final iy belongs to ii, cooked rice, not a stray suffix.
Dia completes meo dia and fixes the meal at midday. The physical line break is kept.
Hiruma is hiru no aida, the daytime interval. The Portuguese narrows it to the midday period in this gloss.

runs.text: ¶ Item, Comer do meo dia de trabalhado-

lines.note: Item gives a workers' midday meal as another sense. Trabalhado continues into trabalhadores.
Res completes trabalhadores. B marks the register of this meal sense, not an initial of a further word.

runs.text: Modo de emburilhar com tiras de

lines.note: Hirumaki is a wrapping method using strips. Preserve emburilhar, also seen on the previous page, rather than silently modernize it.

runs.text: papel, ou outra couſa ao comprido deixando al-

lines.note: Paper or other material is wound along the length while leaving spaces. Al begins the abbreviated plural below.
Gũs completes algũs, with some spaces left open. The description clarifies that the wrapping is not continuous coverage.
Hirumu is slackening or losing courage. Afroxar fits both the visible f and the paired acouardarſe; Atroxar was OCR damage.
Hirune is sleeping during the daytime rest period. Polla ſesta is preserved as the printed Portuguese expression.
Hiru-nusubito is a brazen daytime thief. Ladrão and deſaforado restore the coherent Portuguese gloss without changing its historical spelling.
Hisabisa to is equated with hisashū, a long time. The scan supports a caron on the final u; the explanatory i is not kana material.
Auendo muito tempo restates the elapsed-time sense. It continues the preceding adverb rather than defining a separate noun.

runs.text: He palaura que entra em com-

lines.note: Hisakata is marked poetic. The explanation treats it as a combining expression, consistent with its use as a conventional poetic epithet.

runs.text: poſição com outras, quer dizer ceo, ou couſa

lines.note: It combines with other words and means heaven or something celestial. Outras restores the damaged initial vowel without changing the explanation.
Hisakata no tsuki no hikari is the example, the light of the heavenly moon. The repeated headword resolves the badly read bilacatano.
The Portuguese translates the moonlight expression explicitly as celestial. Lũa's tilde remains in place as printed.

runs.text: Hũa aruoreſinha de cuja cinza fazẽ

lines.note: Hisakaki is a small tree whose ashes are used for lye. The damaged initial Fi is supported by the tree name and NINJAL, not by modernizing its orthography.
Barrela supplies the lye or washing liquor made from those ashes. It completes the tree's practical-use description.

runs.text: Hum vaſo de pao pera dar agoa co-

lines.note: Hisage is a wooden water vessel. The damaged vowel is a, matching the implement name and the alphabetical sequence.
Como gumil compares it with a ewer. The historical gumil form is retained rather than replaced with a modern dictionary form.
Hisagi is a tree name. Enlargement supports final i in Fiſagui, rather than the first-pass j; the spelling is not normalized to modern hisagi.
Hisashi is a small extension to a house. The initial F was misrecognized as B, but the rest of the name and architectural sense are clear.

runs.text: nuado, ou pegado com o meſmo telhado.

lines.note: The extension shares or adjoins the same roof. This specifies the architectural relation of the hisashi.

runs.text: Couſa antigua, ou de muito tempo.

lines.note: Hisashii means old or of long duration. It is unrelated to the preceding eaves noun despite their similar spelling.
Hisashisa is the nominal derivative, duration or long standing. Its indentation associates it with the adjective.
Hisashū is the contracted adverb. The caron on u is visible and is not replaced by a grave merely from the earlier draft.
Hisō here denotes esteem or treasuring. Mono wo hisō suru is the corresponding verbal expression; retain the short s in the locally aligned OCR.

runs.text: timar, ou prezar muito algũa couſa. ¶

lines.note: The gloss means valuing something highly. Go begins the honorific expression continued below.
Go-hisō na mono naredomo kudasareyo asks for something despite its being treasured. The garbled hsôna is restored to fisǒna from the visible types and repeated noun.

runs.text: inda que ſeja couſa que eſtimaes muito, daima.

lines.note: Although you esteem it greatly, give it to me: seja supplies the concessive construction. Daima is the printed fused pronoun expression.
The separate hisō is rosalgar, an arsenic substance. It must not be merged semantically with esteem despite identical romanization.
Hisoka na means secret. Na marks the adjectival form, with the ni adverb following next.
Hisoka ni means secretly. Adu. is the Portuguese grammatical label, not Japanese reading material.
Hisōden names a heaven or cosmological realm. The compact printed word is retained rather than split around its marked o.

Fisofifisǒ names another heaven, recognizably related to the Buddhist neither-perception-nor-nonperception expression. Preserve the missing first long-vowel mark rather than silently emend the printed form.
Hisomeru means quieting or suppressing. Sanco is retained in the example pending the continuation, not replaced with a guessed modern noun.
Wo hisomete kiku is listening with restrained stillness. The Portuguese explicitly describes great attention or quiet.
Attention and quiet complete that example. Mayu wo hisomuru introduces knitting the brows, another sense of the same verb.

runs.text: Fazer rugas na teſta, como quem lhe não agra-

lines.note: The brows create forehead wrinkles as when something displeases a person. The definition explains the expression rather than the literal hiding of eyebrows.
Da completes agrada, the thing not being pleasing. This closes the frowning example.
Hisomeku is making a subdued murmur. Burburi begins the Portuguese word for a low hubbub below.
Nha completes burburinha, qualified by caladamente. The sound is quiet, not complete silence.
Hisō na is something highly valued or treasured. It derives from the esteem entry, not the arsenic or heaven homonyms.
Hisō ni is the adverbial counterpart. The short grammatical gloss refers back to the valued or treasured sense.
Hisoru describes a board bending or warping in the sun. The physical deformation precedes a projectile sense.
Empenar restates warping. Item then describes an arrow glancing or deflecting, preserving the historical Reſuelar form.

runs.text: que dà no capecete, ou peito darmas, &c.

lines.note: The arrow strikes a helmet or breastplate. Preserve capecete as printed rather than supply modern capacete.
Hissabaku is managing or putting in order. The doubled s is recovered where OCR produced ſt, consistent with the visible types and verb.
Managing a household is the first example. The next sense is free, skilled handling of weapons.

runs.text: te, & com deſtreza as armas como Catana,

lines.note: Katana exemplifies weapons handled dexterously. This Japanese term is embedded in Portuguese syntax.
Naginata completes the weapons list. Ito wo hissabaku then shifts to sorting thread; the thread gloss resolves OCR's Irouo as Itouo.

runs.text: Deſempeçar, & amanhar bem o fio das linhas.

lines.note: The action is disentangling and properly arranging thread. That confirms ito rather than iro, colour, in the preceding example.
Hissageru means carrying something suspended from the hand. The repeated s-types are not a t, as the OCR draft suggested.

Chū ni mono wo hissaguru describes suspending something in mid-air. Enlargement and the parallel Portuguese gloss support ni in Chùni; the damaged vowel mark is retained as transcribed rather than silently reconstructed.

runs.text: Ter dependurada algũa couſa da mão no ar.

lines.note: The object hangs from the hand in the air. This gives the spatial relation intended by the previous Japanese example.

runs.text: Fiſſaqi, u, aita. i, fiqiſaqi, u.

lines.note: Hissaku is explicitly equated with hikisaku, tearing apart. The contracted prefix explains the doubled s rather than requiring a separate lexical hypothesis.
The tearing is forceful, or a breaking into pieces. Deſpedaçar restores the damaged final vowel in the Portuguese infinitive.
Hissobameru means turning something by pulling it. The doubled consonant is restored from the scan and headword comparison.
A horse is the object of the pulling-and-turning action. This is an example rather than an exclusive definition.
Hissoku is remaining hidden or confined. Encerrado repairs the draft's garbled division and confirms the seclusion sense.

runs.text: retraido não ſaindo a publico. Vt,

lines.note: The person stays withdrawn and does not appear publicly. ſaindo is sair, going out, not an f-initial verb.
Suru completes hissoku suru. It is a body continuation, not a separate headword.
Hissoroyeru means gathering or arranging in order. The repeated por in por por ordem is grammatically possible and retained.
People arranged in a row illustrate the ordering. Fieira preserves the period Portuguese spelling.
Hissukumeru is forcing or constraining. NINJAL and the scan support the headword where OCR produced an impossible btſe cluster.
Hissuguru means selecting the best. Eſcolher restores the s-type misread as l; milhor remains the printed historical vowel.
Hissui is inevitable decline, explained as kanarazu otoroyuru. It introduces a compound-only expression continued below.

runs.text: do: não ſe vſa ſe não composto. Vt,

lines.note: The dictionary says it is not used alone, only in combination. Xǒxa begins the prosperity-and-decline expression on the next page.
Printed catchword anticipating the opening of f199; verified against that scan. Preserved outside body text with its original stable ID.
